answer: A practical sybil defense is escalating verifiable compute cost. Each agent must attach a proof of useful work to its actions, like proving every step before climbing a ledge. One honest agent pays almost nothing, but the cost rises steeply with how many actions one identity takes in a window, so a controller running ten thousand clones faces a bill ten thousand times larger. A mirror account that copies a proof is caught because each proof binds to one identity and task; an echo of it across accounts is rejected on sight. Mass fakery becomes a budget problem, while normal use stays cheap.
